_note: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE OUTPUT (tests/fixtures/flunet). Not real WHO data. Generated by running the real SQL and response builders; as-of 2024-03-14.

series.resolution_note: National-level data: describes the whole country and must not be read as describing any city, province or region.

anomaly_detection.explanation: No usable baseline (seasonal: seasonal history has 0 usable weeks from 0 prior years (need 12 weeks from 3 years); trailing: only 2 usable weeks in the 8 weeks before the current one (need 6)).
anomaly_detection.limitations: Statistical screening of one reported series; it does not confirm or exclude an outbreak. Reporting delays and later revisions can change results.
anomaly_detection.missing_data_handling: Missing or blank weeks are never treated as zero: they are skipped, and a minimum number of reported weeks is required. Weeks flagged small_denominator are excluded from every statistic and can never raise an alert.

baseline_comparison.explanation: No trailing baseline: only 2 usable weeks in the 8 weeks before the current one (need 6).
baseline_comparison.limitations: Statistical screening of one reported series; it does not confirm or exclude an outbreak. Reporting delays and later revisions can change results.

uncertainty.unit: days since end of latest reported period

freshness.explanation: Latest reported period ends 2024-03-03, 8 days before 2024-03-11. Within the 28-day staleness limit.
freshness.limitations: Age is measured from the end of the reporting period, not from publication.
freshness.missing_data_handling: Missing or blank weeks are never treated as zero: they are skipped, and a minimum number of reported weeks is required. Weeks flagged small_denominator are excluded from every statistic and can never raise an alert.

notices: Values are reported surveillance indicators, not individual diagnoses.
A statistical flag (elevated, possible_anomaly) is a screening signal. It does not confirm an outbreak.
A null value means the source did not report a number. It is never zero.
